episode.subject: sea turtle underwater
episode.title: A beak for the corner
episode.body: I reached the sponge at the back of the crack and bit off a piece. Pulled my head out. Went straight back for the part I had missed. The narrow face is useful; the determination is excessive.

proposals.visibleScene: Hawksbill turtle lies diagonally over a reef recess, narrow head turned left into attached growth. One front flipper braces nearby; mottled shell and rear flippers legible. NPS caption identifies sponge biting. Mouthful separation is not resolved.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Sequence of biting off a piece, withdrawing, returning and determination is fictional. Still establishes the bite setup, not a documented two-bite sequence. No torn long strip, fish, eggs or second turtle asserted.
proposals.continuity: Recover original slot 2 after childhood I said I was going back and before Still going down. Retain Little Cayman home, avatar and all existing words. Virgin Islands is image provenance for a compatible Caribbean species and reef, not a narrated journey.
proposals.biologyEvidence: NOAA Fisheries identifies Eretmochelys imbricata, reef sponge feeding and sharp narrow mouth reaching into holes and crevices. Primary page opened and relevant text read.
proposals.qualityRisk: Original is 600x422 with hard sun highlights and some softness. Anatomical setup legible, but no assertion it passes lead visual review. Does not earn The attached end because no unraveling strip visible.
